Chapter 10: Sustaining Motivation—Habits for the Long Run
Ever notice how motivation isn’t just a one-time spark? It’s more like a journey—something you have to keep coming back to, reflecting on, and adapting as life unfolds.
So, how do you actually keep that inner drive alive? Let’s talk about a few habits that make all the difference.
First, set goals that truly matter to you. Not just any goals—pick ones that feel meaningful, that challenge you just enough to keep things interesting.
Next, keep track of how far you’ve come. Whether you use a journal, a checklist, or just check in with yourself regularly, noticing your progress helps you see the growth that might otherwise slip by.
Don’t forget to ask for feedback. Sometimes, a fresh perspective from someone else is exactly what you need to course-correct or see things in a new light.
And every now and then, take a moment to remember why you started. Reconnect with your purpose—remind yourself what makes your work or learning truly matter.
Of course, motivation isn’t always steady. There’ll be stretches where you’re full of energy, and others where it’s tough just to get started. When you hit a low point, come back to those core elements—autonomy, mastery, and purpose. They’re like the roots that keep you grounded and help you find your spark again.
Honestly, keeping motivated is a lot like tending a campfire. You can’t just light it once and walk away—every so often, you’ve got to add new fuel, adjust the logs, and give it a gentle poke so it keeps burning bright.
Motivation works the same way. With a little intention and patience, you can keep that fire alive for the long run.
